subject: Priority override matrix: Asteria (AST-4521) — exception request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@asteria.com>, Linda Chan <linda.chan@asteria.com>
Date: 2026-11-08 09:12 PST
Subject: Priority override matrix: Asteria (AST-4521) — exception request

Team —

Quick context: Asteria (AST-4521) is at final procurement and has asked for a scoped exception we don’t currently productize: per-tenant dynamic billing tags + an exceptions API to opt-out of our standard rate-limiter for specific traffic patterns (they have an internal compliance-backed burst window for regulatory reporting). Legal/procurement are ready to sign if we commit to a phased delivery with hard dates.

Why this matters now:
- $1.2M ARR first-year with conservative usage assumptions (HubSpot record linked below).
- They require the exception to be gated behind an audit trail (we can leverage existing telemetry but need a dedicated export).
- Procurement deadline: 2026-11-20 — they will push signature if we can commit to MVP dates.

Ask from Product/Eng: can you evaluate and slot this as a prioritization exception? Specifically we need:
1) A small prioritization matrix (risk/cost/time) with three options: minimal spike (API shim + manual approval), phased feature (API + export + canary), full productization (automated policy + HA).
2) Rough timelines (calendar dates) and minimum engineering headcount to meet the procurement deadline for the phased option.
3) Any gating concerns (security reviews, SOC/KS integration, telemetry retention impact).

Attachments: Asteria_deal_brief.pdf (deal summary), SOW-draft.docx (initial SOW). I’ve also dropped the HubSpot deal link below.

I appreciate a quick turnaround — Ben/ Priyom, could you reply with an initial thumbs-up/concerns by EOD Monday (2026-11-09)? Monica — can you coordinate with CS for the customer acceptance criteria and confirm the compliance export format with Sofia?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Asteria_deal_brief.pdf (1 page summary), SOW-draft.docx (draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@asteria.com>
Date: 2026-11-08 11:03 PST
Subject: Re: Priority override matrix: Asteria (AST-4521) — exception request

Kim —

Thanks for the context. High level reaction: doable as a phased approach but we need to be explicit about SLO/rollback and how we handle telemetry. Two quick clarifying Qs so we can size the spike:
- Expected peak RPS during their "burst window"? (even ballpark helps).
- Do they expect traffic routed to a dedicated pool or just policy-level exceptions on shared infra?

Proposal: I can staff a 2-week discovery spike (1 SWE + 0.5 SRE + PM support) to prototype an API shim and export hook. Deliverable would be a tech-debt-minimizing pattern we can ship behind a feature flag and use for the canary. If procurement requires calendar commitments, we can propose a canary date 4 weeks after spike completion.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer (Deals)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Priority override matrix: Asteria (AST-4521) — exception request

Thanks — I pulled the attachments and reviewed the deal brief. I sketched a lightweight matrix (attached: priority-matrix.xlsx) with three options and tradeoffs. High level summary below:

Option A — API Shim (low risk)
- Scope: Server-side policy layer that accepts per-tenant tag + override token; manual approval required.
- Timeline: 2-week spike + 2-week canary = ~4 weeks to customer canary.
- Cost: Low infra delta; higher manual ops overhead.
- Risk: Audit trail is dependent on current logs; we’ll need a curated export for compliance.

Option B — Phased feature (recommended)
- Scope: API + dedicated export stream (S3/secure transfer) + automated approval hooks; content TTL and trace metadata baked in.
- Timeline: 2-week spike + 3-week implementation + 2-week canary = ~7 weeks.
- Cost: Medium; requires small infra changes and retention config.
- Risk: Moderate; needs security review and a quick SOC checklist.

Option C — Productize (long term)
- Scope: Fully-managed policy, UI controls, billing tags baked into metering.
- Timeline: 3+ months.
- Cost: High; product roadmap item.
- Risk: Low at runtime, higher delivery cost.

Open items for legal/security: export format confirmation (Monica/Sofia), data residency for export (Asteria asked for EU mirroring if requested by auditors), and whether the override token must be stored in customer KMS or our KMS.

I attached priority-matrix.xlsx (tabbed by risk/cost/timeline) and marked required gating tasks. If the customer accepts phased approach (Option B) I can scope JIRA tickets and propose sprint allocation.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm resource availability for a 2-week spike starting 2026-11-15? Monica, please sync with Sofia on export format and confirm procurement flexibility.

—Priyom
Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-10 14:22 EST
Subject: Re: Priority override matrix: Asteria (AST-4521) — exception request

Kim —

Appreciate the quick turn. We discussed internally and Asteria is comfortable with the phased approach (Option B) provided we have a canary in production within ~8 weeks and a formal audit export delivered with the canary. Procurement can sign with that commitment.

Answers to clarifying Qs:
- Burst window: typically up to 3x baseline RPS for a 4-hour nightly reporting window — absolute numbers shared in the attached deal brief.
- Routing: we are fine with policy-level exceptions on shared infra so long as audit export is immutable and stored with our retention policy.

Please let us know proposed canary dates after you finalize internal capacity. We can be flexible on go-live as long as the canary and export are in place.

—Sofia Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering
Asteria Bank
